about: PostgreSQL 17 built-in vocabulary. Also used for the Postgres-family engines the app maps to this dialect; keep to PostgreSQL's own vocabulary.

functions.name: array_agg
functions.summary: Collects the input values, including nulls, into an array. Add ORDER BY inside the call to control element order.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to collect; arrays are collected into an array of one more dimension.

functions.name: string_agg
functions.summary: Concatenates the non-null input values into one string, separated by the delimiter. Add ORDER BY inside the call to control order.

functions.name: json_agg
functions.summary: Collects the input values, including nulls, into a JSON array.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to add to the array; converted with to_json.

functions.name: jsonb_agg
functions.summary: Collects the input values, including nulls, into a JSONB array.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to add to the array; converted with to_jsonb.

functions.name: json_agg_strict
functions.summary: Collects the input values into a JSON array, skipping nulls. (PostgreSQL 16+)

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to add to the array; nulls are skipped.

functions.name: jsonb_agg_strict
functions.summary: Collects the input values into a JSONB array, skipping nulls. (PostgreSQL 16+)

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to add to the array; nulls are skipped.

functions.name: json_object_agg
functions.summary: Collects key/value pairs into a JSON object. Keys must not be null; values may be.

params.name: key
params.doc: The object key; converted to text.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value stored under the key.

functions.name: jsonb_object_agg
functions.summary: Collects key/value pairs into a JSONB object. Keys must not be null; duplicate keys keep the last value.

params.name: key
params.doc: The object key; converted to text.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value stored under the key.

functions.name: jsonb_object_agg_strict
functions.summary: Collects key/value pairs into a JSONB object, skipping pairs whose value is null. (PostgreSQL 16+)

params.name: key
params.doc: The object key; converted to text.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value; pairs with a null value are skipped.

functions.name: jsonb_object_agg_unique
functions.summary: Collects key/value pairs into a JSONB object and raises an error on a duplicate key. (PostgreSQL 16+)

params.name: key
params.doc: The object key; must be unique within the group.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value stored under the key.

functions.name: json_arrayagg
functions.summary: SQL-standard aggregate that collects values into a JSON array; nulls are skipped unless NULL ON NULL is given. (PostgreSQL 16+)

params.name: value [ORDER BY …] [{NULL | ABSENT} ON NULL] [RETURNING type]
params.doc: The value to collect, with optional ordering, null handling and result type.

functions.name: json_objectagg
functions.summary: SQL-standard aggregate that collects key/value pairs into a JSON object. (PostgreSQL 16+)

params.name: key VALUE value [{NULL | ABSENT} ON NULL] [{WITH | WITHOUT} UNIQUE KEYS] [RETURNING type]
params.doc: The key and value of each pair, with optional null handling, uniqueness check and result type.

functions.name: bool_and
functions.summary: Returns true if every non-null input value is true, otherwise false.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The condition to test for each row.

functions.name: bool_or
functions.summary: Returns true if at least one non-null input value is true, otherwise false.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The condition to test for each row.

functions.name: every
functions.summary: SQL-standard equivalent of bool_and: true if every non-null input value is true.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The condition to test for each row.

functions.name: bit_and
functions.summary: Computes the bitwise AND of all non-null input values.

functions.name: bit_or
functions.summary: Computes the bitwise OR of all non-null input values.

functions.name: bit_xor
functions.summary: Computes the bitwise exclusive OR of all non-null input values.

functions.name: any_value
functions.summary: Returns an arbitrary value from the non-null input values. (PostgreSQL 16+)

functions.name: grouping
functions.summary: In a query with GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP or CUBE, returns a bit mask telling which of the listed expressions are not grouped in the current row.

params.name: group_by_expression
params.doc: An expression that appears in the GROUP BY clause.

functions.name: stddev
functions.summary: Historical alias for stddev_samp: the sample standard deviation of the input values.

functions.name: stddev_samp
functions.summary: Returns the sample standard deviation of the non-null input values.

functions.name: stddev_pop
functions.summary: Returns the population standard deviation of the non-null input values.

functions.name: variance
functions.summary: Historical alias for var_samp: the sample variance of the input values.

functions.name: var_samp
functions.summary: Returns the sample variance (square of the sample standard deviation) of the non-null input values.

functions.name: var_pop
functions.summary: Returns the population variance of the non-null input values.

functions.name: corr
functions.summary: Returns the correlation coefficient of the pairs of non-null values.

functions.name: covar_pop
functions.summary: Returns the population covariance of the pairs of non-null values.

functions.name: covar_samp
functions.summary: Returns the sample covariance of the pairs of non-null values.

functions.name: regr_avgx
functions.summary: Returns the average of the independent variable X over pairs where both values are non-null.

functions.name: regr_avgy
functions.summary: Returns the average of the dependent variable Y over pairs where both values are non-null.

functions.name: regr_count
functions.summary: Returns the number of rows in which both inputs are non-null.

functions.name: regr_intercept
functions.summary: Returns the y-intercept of the least-squares-fit linear equation determined by the (X, Y) pairs.

functions.name: regr_r2
functions.summary: Returns the square of the correlation coefficient of the (X, Y) pairs.

functions.name: regr_slope
functions.summary: Returns the slope of the least-squares-fit linear equation determined by the (X, Y) pairs.

functions.name: regr_sxx
functions.summary: Returns the sum of squares of the independent variable: sum(X^2) - sum(X)^2/N.

functions.name: regr_sxy
functions.summary: Returns the sum of products of the independent and dependent variables: sum(X*Y) - sum(X)*sum(Y)/N.

functions.name: regr_syy
functions.summary: Returns the sum of squares of the dependent variable: sum(Y^2) - sum(Y)^2/N.

functions.name: mode
functions.summary: Ordered-set aggregate that returns the most frequent value of the ORDER BY expression, choosing arbitrarily among ties.

functions.name: percentile_cont
functions.summary: Ordered-set aggregate that returns the continuous percentile, interpolating between adjacent values. Use WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY …).

params.name: fraction
params.doc: The percentile to compute, from 0 to 1.

params.name: fractions
params.doc: An array of percentiles; returns an array of results.

functions.name: percentile_disc
functions.summary: Ordered-set aggregate that returns the first input value whose position in the ordering equals or exceeds the fraction. Use WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY …).

params.name: fraction
params.doc: The percentile to compute, from 0 to 1.

params.name: fractions
params.doc: An array of percentiles; returns an array of results.

functions.name: range_agg
functions.summary: Computes the union of the non-null input ranges as a multirange. (PostgreSQL 14+)

functions.name: range_intersect_agg
functions.summary: Computes the intersection of the non-null input ranges or multiranges.

functions.name: xmlagg
functions.summary: Concatenates the non-null XML input values. Add ORDER BY inside the call to control order.

functions.name: nth_value
functions.summary: Returns the value evaluated at the n-th row of the window frame (counting from 1), or null if there is no such row.

params.name: value
params.doc: The expression to evaluate at that row.

params.name: n
params.doc: The row number within the frame, starting at 1.

functions.name: lower
functions.summary: Converts a string to lower case using the database locale. For a range or multirange, returns its lower bound.

params.name: range
params.doc: The range whose lower bound to return; null if empty or unbounded.

functions.name: upper
functions.summary: Converts a string to upper case using the database locale. For a range or multirange, returns its upper bound.

params.name: range
params.doc: The range whose upper bound to return; null if empty or unbounded.

functions.name: length
functions.summary: Returns the number of characters in a string. Also works on bytea (bytes), bit strings (bits) and tsvector (lexemes).

functions.name: char_length
functions.summary: Returns the number of characters in a string.

functions.name: character_length
functions.summary: SQL-standard synonym for char_length: the number of characters in a string.

functions.name: octet_length
functions.summary: Returns the number of bytes in a string or bytea value.

functions.name: bit_length
functions.summary: Returns the number of bits in a string, bytea or bit string.

functions.name: initcap
functions.summary: Converts the first letter of each word to upper case and the rest to lower case. Words are runs of alphanumeric characters.

functions.name: substring
functions.summary: Extracts part of a string by position, by POSIX regular expression, or by SQL regular expression.

params.name: string [FROM start] [FOR count]
params.doc: The string, then the 1-based start position and/or the number of characters to take.

params.name: start
params.doc: The 1-based position of the first character.

params.name: count
params.doc: How many characters to take; defaults to the rest of the string.

params.name: string FROM pattern
params.doc: The string and a POSIX regular expression; returns the first parenthesized group, or the whole match.

params.name: string SIMILAR pattern ESCAPE escape
params.doc: The string, an SQL regular expression and its escape character.

functions.name: substr
functions.summary: Extracts part of a string starting at a 1-based position, optionally limited to count characters.

params.name: start
params.doc: The 1-based position of the first character.

params.name: count
params.doc: How many characters to take; defaults to the rest of the string.

functions.name: left
functions.summary: Returns the first n characters of a string; when n is negative, all but the last |n| characters.

params.name: n
params.doc: How many characters to keep from the start.

functions.name: right
functions.summary: Returns the last n characters of a string; when n is negative, all but the first |n| characters.

params.name: n
params.doc: How many characters to keep from the end.

functions.name: position
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of a substring, or 0 if it is not present.

params.name: substring IN string
params.doc: The text to look for, the keyword IN, then the string to search.

functions.name: strpos
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of a substring, or 0 if it is not present.

functions.name: concat
functions.summary: Concatenates the text of all arguments. Null arguments are ignored.

params.name: value
params.doc: A value to append; nulls are skipped.

functions.name: concat_ws
functions.summary: Concatenates all arguments but the first, separated by the first argument. Null arguments are ignored.

params.name: value
params.doc: A value to append; nulls are skipped.

functions.name: format
functions.summary: Formats arguments into a string using a template with %s (text), %I (identifier) and %L (literal) placeholders, similar to sprintf.
functions.example: format('SELECT * FROM %I WHERE id = %L', tbl, id)

params.name: formatstr
params.doc: The template; %s, %I, %L and %% are replaced in order.

params.name: formatarg
params.doc: A value substituted into the next placeholder.

functions.name: lpad
functions.summary: Pads a string on the left to the given length with fill characters (a space by default). A longer string is truncated on the right.

params.name: fill
params.doc: The characters to pad with; defaults to a space.

functions.name: rpad
functions.summary: Pads a string on the right to the given length with fill characters (a space by default). A longer string is truncated.

params.name: fill
params.doc: The characters to pad with; defaults to a space.

functions.name: trim
functions.summary: Removes the longest run of the given characters (spaces by default) from the start, end or both ends of a string.

params.name: [LEADING | TRAILING | BOTH] [characters] FROM string
params.doc: Which end to trim, the characters to remove, then FROM and the string.

params.name: [LEADING | TRAILING | BOTH] [FROM] string
params.doc: Which end to trim, then the string.

params.name: characters
params.doc: The characters to remove; defaults to a space.

functions.name: btrim
functions.summary: Removes the longest run of the given characters (spaces by default) from both ends of a string.

params.name: characters
params.doc: The characters to remove; defaults to a space.

functions.name: ltrim
functions.summary: Removes the longest run of the given characters (spaces by default) from the start of a string.

params.name: characters
params.doc: The characters to remove; defaults to a space.

functions.name: rtrim
functions.summary: Removes the longest run of the given characters (spaces by default) from the end of a string.

params.name: characters
params.doc: The characters to remove; defaults to a space.

functions.name: repeat
functions.summary: Repeats a string the given number of times.

params.name: number
params.doc: How many times to repeat it.

functions.name: reverse
functions.summary: Reverses the order of the characters in a string.

functions.name: split_part
functions.summary: Splits a string at a delimiter and returns the n-th field (counting from 1). A negative n counts from the end.

params.name: n
params.doc: Which field to return; negative counts from the end.

functions.name: string_to_array
functions.summary: Splits a string at a delimiter into a text array. A null delimiter splits into single characters.

params.name: delimiter
params.doc: The separator; null splits into characters, an empty string yields one element.

params.name: null_string
params.doc: Fields equal to this text become nulls.

functions.name: string_to_table
functions.summary: Splits a string at a delimiter and returns the fields as a set of rows. (PostgreSQL 14+)

params.name: delimiter
params.doc: The separator; null splits into characters.

params.name: null_string
params.doc: Fields equal to this text become nulls.

functions.name: regexp_replace
functions.summary: Replaces substrings that match a POSIX regular expression. Only the first match is replaced unless the g flag or an N of 0 is given.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: replacement
params.doc: The replacement text; \1 to \9 refer to groups, \& to the whole match.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: replacement
params.doc: The replacement text; \1 to \9 refer to groups, \& to the whole match.

params.name: N
params.doc: Which match to replace; 0 replaces all.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

functions.name: regexp_match
functions.summary: Returns the captured substrings of the first match of a POSIX regular expression as a text array, or null if there is no match.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

functions.name: regexp_matches
functions.summary: Returns the captured substrings of each match of a POSIX regular expression as rows of text arrays; use the g flag for every match.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

functions.name: regexp_split_to_table
functions.summary: Splits a string using a POSIX regular expression as the delimiter and returns the pieces as rows.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

functions.name: regexp_split_to_array
functions.summary: Splits a string using a POSIX regular expression as the delimiter and returns the pieces as an array.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

functions.name: regexp_like
functions.summary: Returns true if a POSIX regular expression matches anywhere in the string. (PostgreSQL 15+)

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

functions.name: regexp_count
functions.summary: Counts the matches of a POSIX regular expression in a string. (PostgreSQL 15+)

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

functions.name: regexp_substr
functions.summary: Returns the substring matching the N-th occurrence of a POSIX regular expression, or null if there is none. (PostgreSQL 15+)

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: N
params.doc: Which occurrence to return; defaults to 1.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

params.name: subexpr
params.doc: Which parenthesized group to return; 0 means the whole match.

functions.name: regexp_instr
functions.summary: Returns the position of the N-th match of a POSIX regular expression, or 0 if there is none. (PostgreSQL 15+)

params.name: pattern
params.doc: The POSIX regular expression to match.

params.name: N
params.doc: Which occurrence to find; defaults to 1.

params.name: endoption
params.doc: 0 returns the match's first character, 1 the position just after it.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Optional flag letters, such as i for case-insensitive or g for every match.

params.name: subexpr
params.doc: Which parenthesized group to locate; 0 means the whole match.

functions.name: starts_with
functions.summary: Returns true if a string starts with the given prefix.

functions.name: to_hex
functions.summary: Converts an integer to its hexadecimal text representation.

functions.name: translate
functions.summary: Replaces each character in the string that matches a character in from with the corresponding character in to; extra from characters are deleted.

functions.name: overlay
functions.summary: Replaces the part of a string starting at a position (and spanning count characters) with a new substring.

params.name: string PLACING newsubstring FROM start [FOR count]
params.doc: The string, the replacement, its 1-based start and optionally how many characters to replace.

functions.name: chr
functions.summary: Returns the character with the given code point (in UTF-8) or byte value.

functions.name: ascii
functions.summary: Returns the numeric code of the first character of a string (the Unicode code point in UTF-8).

functions.name: quote_ident
functions.summary: Returns a string quoted as an SQL identifier, adding double quotes only when needed.

functions.name: quote_literal
functions.summary: Returns a value quoted as an SQL string literal, doubling embedded quotes and backslashes. Returns null for null input.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to quote; non-text values are cast to text.

functions.name: quote_nullable
functions.summary: Like quote_literal, but returns the unquoted string NULL for a null input.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to quote; null becomes NULL.

functions.name: unistr
functions.summary: Evaluates Unicode escapes (\XXXX, \+XXXXXX, \uXXXX, \UXXXXXXXX) in a string. (PostgreSQL 14+)

functions.name: normalize
functions.summary: Converts a string to the given Unicode normalization form (NFC by default). The database encoding must be UTF8.

params.name: form
params.doc: The normalization form: NFC, NFD, NFKC or NFKD.

functions.name: parse_ident
functions.summary: Splits a qualified identifier such as schema.table into an array of identifiers, removing quotes.

params.name: strict_mode
params.doc: When false, extra characters after the identifier are ignored; defaults to true.

functions.name: convert_from
functions.summary: Converts bytes in the given encoding to text in the database encoding.

params.name: src_encoding
params.doc: The source encoding, such as 'UTF8' or 'LATIN1'.

functions.name: convert_to
functions.summary: Converts text to bytes in the given encoding.

params.name: dest_encoding
params.doc: The target encoding, such as 'UTF8' or 'LATIN1'.

functions.name: pg_client_encoding
functions.summary: Returns the name of the current client encoding.

functions.name: encode
functions.summary: Encodes binary data into text using the base64, escape or hex format.

functions.name: decode
functions.summary: Decodes text produced by encode back into binary data.

functions.name: md5
functions.summary: Computes the MD5 hash of a string or bytea value and returns it as 32 hexadecimal digits.

functions.name: sha224
functions.summary: Computes the SHA-224 hash of binary data. Convert text with convert_to or a ::bytea cast first.

functions.name: sha256
functions.summary: Computes the SHA-256 hash of binary data. Convert text with convert_to or a ::bytea cast first.

functions.name: sha384
functions.summary: Computes the SHA-384 hash of binary data. Convert text with convert_to or a ::bytea cast first.

functions.name: sha512
functions.summary: Computes the SHA-512 hash of binary data. Convert text with convert_to or a ::bytea cast first.

functions.name: round
functions.summary: Rounds to the nearest integer, or to s decimal places for numeric input. Ties round away from zero for numeric and to even for double precision.

params.name: s
params.doc: Decimal places to keep (numeric only); negative rounds left of the point.

functions.name: trunc
functions.summary: Truncates toward zero, or to s decimal places for numeric input. For macaddr, sets the last three bytes to zero.

functions.name: ceil
functions.summary: Returns the nearest integer greater than or equal to the argument.

functions.name: ceiling
functions.summary: Returns the nearest integer greater than or equal to the argument (same as ceil).

functions.name: floor
functions.summary: Returns the nearest integer less than or equal to the argument.

functions.name: mod
functions.summary: Returns the remainder of y divided by x.

functions.name: div
functions.summary: Returns the integer quotient of y divided by x, truncated toward zero.

functions.name: power
functions.summary: Raises a to the power of b.

functions.name: sqrt
functions.summary: Returns the square root.

functions.name: cbrt
functions.summary: Returns the cube root.

functions.name: exp
functions.summary: Returns e raised to the given power.

functions.name: ln
functions.summary: Returns the natural logarithm.

functions.name: log
functions.summary: Returns the base-10 logarithm of x, or the logarithm of x to base b when two arguments are given.

functions.name: log10
functions.summary: Returns the base-10 logarithm.

functions.name: pi
functions.summary: Returns the constant pi.

functions.name: random
functions.summary: Returns a random value in the range 0.0 <= x < 1.0, or a random value between min and max inclusive. (min/max form: PostgreSQL 17+)

functions.name: random_normal
functions.summary: Returns a random value from the normal distribution with the given mean and standard deviation. (PostgreSQL 16+)

functions.name: setseed
functions.summary: Sets the seed for later random() and random_normal() calls in this session.

functions.name: sign
functions.summary: Returns -1, 0 or +1 depending on the sign of the argument.

functions.name: degrees
functions.summary: Converts radians to degrees.

functions.name: radians
functions.summary: Converts degrees to radians.

functions.name: gcd
functions.summary: Returns the greatest common divisor; 0 if both inputs are zero.

functions.name: lcm
functions.summary: Returns the least common multiple; 0 if either input is zero.

functions.name: factorial
functions.summary: Returns the factorial of a non-negative integer.

functions.name: scale
functions.summary: Returns the number of decimal digits in the fractional part of a numeric value.

functions.name: min_scale
functions.summary: Returns the smallest scale needed to represent a numeric value exactly.

functions.name: trim_scale
functions.summary: Removes trailing zeroes from the fractional part of a numeric value.

functions.name: width_bucket
functions.summary: Returns the number of the bucket an operand falls in, for equal-width buckets between low and high, or for buckets bounded by a sorted thresholds array.

params.name: low
params.doc: The lower bound of the first bucket.

params.name: high
params.doc: The upper bound of the last bucket.

params.name: thresholds
params.doc: A sorted array of bucket lower bounds.

functions.name: sin
functions.summary: Returns the sine of an angle in radians.

functions.name: cos
functions.summary: Returns the cosine of an angle in radians.

functions.name: tan
functions.summary: Returns the tangent of an angle in radians.

functions.name: cot
functions.summary: Returns the cotangent of an angle in radians.

functions.name: asin
functions.summary: Returns the inverse sine, in radians.

functions.name: acos
functions.summary: Returns the inverse cosine, in radians.

functions.name: atan
functions.summary: Returns the inverse tangent, in radians.

functions.name: sind
functions.summary: Returns the sine of an angle in degrees.

functions.name: cosd
functions.summary: Returns the cosine of an angle in degrees.

functions.name: tand
functions.summary: Returns the tangent of an angle in degrees.

functions.name: cotd
functions.summary: Returns the cotangent of an angle in degrees.

functions.name: asind
functions.summary: Returns the inverse sine, in degrees.

functions.name: acosd
functions.summary: Returns the inverse cosine, in degrees.

functions.name: atand
functions.summary: Returns the inverse tangent, in degrees.

functions.name: sinh
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic sine.

functions.name: cosh
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic cosine.

functions.name: tanh
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic tangent.

functions.name: asinh
functions.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine.

functions.name: acosh
functions.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine.

functions.name: atanh
functions.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent.

functions.name: atan2
functions.summary: Returns the inverse tangent of y/x, in radians, using the signs of both to pick the quadrant.

functions.name: atan2d
functions.summary: Returns the inverse tangent of y/x, in degrees, using the signs of both to pick the quadrant.

functions.name: greatest
functions.summary: Returns the largest of the arguments, ignoring nulls. Returns null only if every argument is null.

functions.name: least
functions.summary: Returns the smallest of the arguments, ignoring nulls. Returns null only if every argument is null.

functions.name: num_nulls
functions.summary: Returns the number of null arguments.

functions.name: num_nonnulls
functions.summary: Returns the number of non-null arguments.

functions.name: now
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time at the start of the current transaction.

functions.name: current_date
functions.summary: Returns the current date at the start of the current transaction. Written without parentheses.

functions.name: current_time
functions.summary: Returns the current time of day with time zone at the start of the current transaction. Written without parentheses unless a precision is given.

params.name: precision
params.doc: Fractional-second digits to keep, from 0 to 6.

functions.name: current_timestamp
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time with time zone at the start of the current transaction; same as now(). Written without parentheses unless a precision is given.

params.name: precision
params.doc: Fractional-second digits to keep, from 0 to 6.

functions.name: localtime
functions.summary: Returns the current time of day without time zone at the start of the current transaction.

params.name: precision
params.doc: Fractional-second digits to keep, from 0 to 6.

functions.name: localtimestamp
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time without time zone at the start of the current transaction.

params.name: precision
params.doc: Fractional-second digits to keep, from 0 to 6.

functions.name: clock_timestamp
functions.summary: Returns the actual current date and time, which changes even within a single statement.

functions.name: statement_timestamp
functions.summary: Returns the date and time at the start of the current statement.

functions.name: transaction_timestamp
functions.summary: Returns the date and time at the start of the current transaction; same as now().

functions.name: timeofday
functions.summary: Returns the actual current date and time as formatted text, like clock_timestamp().

functions.name: date_trunc

functions.name: make_date

functions.name: make_time

functions.name: justify_hours

functions.name: isfinite

params.name: time_zone

functions.name: date_subtract

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: The time zone used for the arithmetic; defaults to the session time zone.

params.name: zone

params.name: timezone
params.doc: For timestamptz, the time zone for the arithmetic. (PostgreSQL 16+)

functions.name: pg_sleep
functions.summary: Delays the current session for the given number of seconds.

params.doc: How long to sleep; fractions are allowed.

functions.name: pg_sleep_for

functions.name: pg_sleep_until

params.name: value

functions.name: to_date
functions.summary: Converts a string to a date using a template.

params.name: format
params.doc: The template describing the input, such as 'DD Mon YYYY'.

functions.name: to_number
functions.summary: Converts a string to a numeric value using a template.

params.name: format
params.doc: The template describing the input, such as '99G999D9S'.

functions.name: to_timestamp
functions.summary: Converts a Unix epoch (seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC) to a timestamp with time zone, or parses a string with a template.

params.name: format

functions.summary: Builds a JSONB array from a variadic list of values of any type.

params.name: value

params.name: values

functions.name: json_scalar

params.name: path_expression [PASSING …] [RETURNING type] [ON EMPTY] [ON ERROR]
params.doc: The path plus optional variables, result type and empty/error behavior.

params.doc: Adds the item when it does not exist; defaults to true.

keywords.name: LIMIT
keywords.doc: Returns at most the given number of rows. LIMIT ALL or LIMIT with a null count means no limit.
keywords.syntax: LIMIT { count | ALL }

keywords.name: OFFSET
keywords.doc: Skips the given number of rows before returning results.
keywords.syntax: OFFSET start [ ROW | ROWS ]

keywords.name: FETCH
keywords.doc: In SELECT, the SQL-standard way to limit rows (FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY). In PL/pgSQL or with cursors, retrieves rows from a cursor.
keywords.syntax: FETCH { FIRST | NEXT } [ count ] { ROW | ROWS } { ONLY | WITH TIES }

keywords.name: FETCH FIRST
keywords.doc: Limits the number of rows returned, like LIMIT.
keywords.syntax: FETCH FIRST [ count ] { ROW | ROWS } { ONLY | WITH TIES }

keywords.name: FETCH NEXT
keywords.doc: Limits the number of rows returned, like LIMIT; NEXT and FIRST are synonyms.
keywords.syntax: FETCH NEXT [ count ] { ROW | ROWS } { ONLY | WITH TIES }

keywords.name: FIRST
keywords.doc: Used in FETCH FIRST, NULLS FIRST and cursor FETCH to refer to the first row(s).

keywords.name: NEXT
keywords.doc: Used in FETCH NEXT and cursor FETCH to refer to the following row(s).

keywords.name: LAST
keywords.doc: Used in NULLS LAST and cursor FETCH LAST to refer to the last position.

keywords.name: ONLY
keywords.doc: In FETCH FIRST … ROWS ONLY, ends the row limit. Before a table name, excludes inheritance children and partitions.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FROM ONLY table

keywords.name: WITH TIES
keywords.doc: In FETCH FIRST, also returns rows that tie with the last row by the ORDER BY key.
keywords.syntax: FETCH FIRST n ROWS WITH TIES

keywords.name: TIES
keywords.doc: Used in FETCH FIRST … WITH TIES.

keywords.name: RETURNING
keywords.doc: Returns values from rows changed by INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE.
keywords.syntax: INSERT … RETURNING * | expression [ AS name ] [, …]

keywords.name: ILIKE
keywords.doc: Case-insensitive pattern match using % and _ wildcards.
keywords.syntax: string [ NOT ] ILIKE pattern [ ESCAPE char ]

keywords.name: SIMILAR TO
keywords.doc: Matches a string against an SQL regular expression, which mixes LIKE wildcards with regex operators.
keywords.syntax: string [ NOT ] SIMILAR TO pattern [ ESCAPE char ]

keywords.name: SIMILAR
keywords.doc: Used in SIMILAR TO pattern matching.

keywords.name: LATERAL
keywords.doc: Lets a subquery or function in FROM refer to columns of earlier FROM items.
keywords.syntax: FROM a, LATERAL (SELECT … WHERE x = a.id) s

keywords.name: WINDOW
keywords.doc: Defines named window specifications that OVER clauses can reference.
keywords.syntax: WINDOW name AS ( [ PARTITION BY … ] [ ORDER BY … ] [ frame ] )

keywords.name: FILTER
keywords.doc: Restricts the rows an aggregate processes.
keywords.syntax: aggregate(…) FILTER ( WHERE condition )

keywords.name: WITHIN GROUP
keywords.doc: Supplies the ordering for an ordered-set aggregate such as percentile_cont or mode.
keywords.syntax: aggregate(args) WITHIN GROUP ( ORDER BY sort_expression )

keywords.name: WITHIN
keywords.doc: Used in WITHIN GROUP for ordered-set aggregates.

keywords.name: RECURSIVE
keywords.doc: Allows a WITH query to refer to its own output, for hierarchies and graph traversal.
keywords.syntax: WITH RECURSIVE name AS ( non_recursive_term UNION [ ALL ] recursive_term )

keywords.name: WITH RECURSIVE
keywords.doc: Starts a common table expression that can refer to its own output.
keywords.syntax: WITH RECURSIVE name [ ( columns ) ] AS ( … UNION [ ALL ] … )

keywords.name: TEMP
keywords.doc: Short for TEMPORARY: the object exists only for the current session.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TEMP TABLE name ( … )

keywords.name: TEMPORARY
keywords.doc: Creates an object that is dropped automatically at the end of the session (or transaction, with ON COMMIT DROP).
keywords.syntax: CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE name ( … ) [ ON COMMIT { PRESERVE ROWS | DELETE ROWS | DROP } ]

keywords.name: UNLOGGED
keywords.doc: Creates a table whose data is not written to the write-ahead log: faster, but truncated after a crash and not replicated.
keywords.syntax: CREATE UNLOGGED TABLE name ( … )

keywords.name: IF
keywords.doc: Used in IF EXISTS / IF NOT EXISTS, and as a PL/pgSQL conditional statement.
keywords.syntax: IF condition THEN … [ ELSIF … ] [ ELSE … ] END IF;

keywords.name: IF EXISTS
keywords.doc: Makes DROP or ALTER succeed with a notice instead of an error when the object does not exist.
keywords.syntax: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS name

keywords.name: IF NOT EXISTS
keywords.doc: Makes CREATE succeed with a notice instead of an error when the object already exists.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS name ( … )

keywords.name: CASCADE
keywords.doc: Also drops or truncates objects that depend on the target, or deletes/updates referencing rows in a foreign key action.
keywords.syntax: DROP TABLE name CASCADE

keywords.name: RESTRICT
keywords.doc: Refuses to drop the object if anything depends on it (the default).
keywords.syntax: DROP TABLE name RESTRICT

keywords.name: TRUNCATE
keywords.doc: Quickly removes all rows from one or more tables.
keywords.syntax: TRUNCATE [ TABLE ] [ ONLY ] name [, …] [ RESTART IDENTITY | CONTINUE IDENTITY ] [ CASCADE | RESTRICT ]

keywords.name: SCHEMA
keywords.doc: A namespace that contains tables, views, functions and other objects.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SCHEMA [ IF NOT EXISTS ] name [ AUTHORIZATION role ]

keywords.name: DATABASE
keywords.doc: A named collection of schemas; each connection works in one database.
keywords.syntax: CREATE DATABASE name [ [ WITH ] OWNER role ENCODING … TEMPLATE … ]

keywords.name: SEQUENCE
keywords.doc: A generator of unique integer values, used by serial and identity columns.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SEQUENCE name [ INCREMENT BY n ] [ MINVALUE n ] [ MAXVALUE n ] [ START WITH n ] [ CACHE n ] [ [ NO ] CYCLE ]

keywords.name: FUNCTION
keywords.doc: A stored routine that returns a value or set, callable in expressions.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] FUNCTION name ( args ) RETURNS type LANGUAGE lang AS $$ … $$

keywords.name: PROCEDURE
keywords.doc: A stored routine invoked with CALL that can commit or roll back transactions.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] PROCEDURE name ( args ) LANGUAGE lang AS $$ … $$

keywords.name: OR REPLACE
keywords.doc: Replaces an existing function, procedure, view, trigger or rule of the same name instead of failing.
keywords.syntax: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION …

keywords.name: RETURNS
keywords.doc: Declares the return type of a function, such as a type, SETOF type, TABLE (…) or trigger.
keywords.syntax: RETURNS { type | SETOF type | TABLE ( column type [, …] ) }

keywords.name: SETOF
keywords.doc: Declares that a function returns a set of rows of the given type.
keywords.syntax: RETURNS SETOF type

keywords.name: LANGUAGE
keywords.doc: Names the language a function or procedure body is written in, such as sql or plpgsql.
keywords.syntax: LANGUAGE { sql | plpgsql | … }

keywords.name: IMMUTABLE
keywords.doc: Declares that a function always returns the same result for the same arguments and does not access the database.

keywords.name: STABLE
keywords.doc: Declares that a function returns the same result for the same arguments within a single statement.

keywords.name: VOLATILE
keywords.doc: Declares that a function's result can change even within a statement (the default), so it is re-evaluated every call.

keywords.name: STRICT
keywords.doc: In a function definition, returns null automatically when any argument is null. In PL/pgSQL SELECT INTO, requires exactly one row.

keywords.name: SECURITY DEFINER
keywords.doc: Runs a function with the privileges of its owner rather than its caller.

keywords.name: SECURITY INVOKER
keywords.doc: Runs a function with the privileges of its caller (the default).

keywords.name: PARALLEL
keywords.doc: Declares whether a function is safe to run in parallel workers: SAFE, RESTRICTED or UNSAFE.
keywords.syntax: PARALLEL { UNSAFE | RESTRICTED | SAFE }

keywords.name: VARIADIC
keywords.doc: Marks the last function parameter as accepting any number of arguments, collected into an array.
keywords.syntax: CREATE FUNCTION f ( VARIADIC args type[] ) …

keywords.name: INOUT
keywords.doc: Declares a function parameter that is both input and output.

keywords.name: OUT
keywords.doc: Declares a function output parameter, which becomes part of the result row.

keywords.name: ATOMIC
keywords.doc: Begins an SQL-standard function or procedure body that is parsed at definition time.
keywords.syntax: BEGIN ATOMIC statements; … END

keywords.name: DO
keywords.doc: Executes an anonymous code block, by default in PL/pgSQL. Also used in ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING / DO UPDATE.
keywords.syntax: DO [ LANGUAGE lang ] $$ … $$

keywords.name: CALL
keywords.doc: Invokes a stored procedure.
keywords.syntax: CALL name ( [ argument ] [, …] )

keywords.name: DECLARE
keywords.doc: Starts the variable declaration section of a PL/pgSQL block, or declares a cursor in SQL.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE name [ BINARY ] [ SCROLL ] CURSOR [ WITH HOLD ] FOR query

keywords.name: EXECUTE
keywords.doc: Runs a prepared statement, or in PL/pgSQL runs a dynamically built command string.
keywords.syntax: EXECUTE command_string [ INTO target ] [ USING expression [, …] ]

keywords.name: PERFORM
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, runs a query and discards its result.
keywords.syntax: PERFORM query;

keywords.name: RAISE
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, reports a message or raises an error.
keywords.syntax: RAISE [ DEBUG | LOG | INFO | NOTICE | WARNING | EXCEPTION ] 'format' [, expression …] [ USING option = value ]

keywords.name: NOTICE
keywords.doc: A message level for RAISE, sent to the client without stopping execution.
keywords.syntax: RAISE NOTICE 'message %', value;

keywords.name: WARNING
keywords.doc: A message level for RAISE, sent to the client without stopping execution.
keywords.syntax: RAISE WARNING 'message';

keywords.name: EXCEPTION
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, starts the error-handling section of a block, or as a RAISE level raises an error.
keywords.syntax: BEGIN … EXCEPTION WHEN condition THEN … END;

keywords.name: ASSERT
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, raises an error if a condition is not true.
keywords.syntax: ASSERT condition [, message];

keywords.name: LOOP
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, starts an unconditional loop that runs until EXIT or RETURN.
keywords.syntax: [ <<label>> ] LOOP statements END LOOP [ label ];

keywords.name: FOR
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, loops over an integer range or query rows. In SELECT, starts a row-locking clause such as FOR UPDATE.
keywords.syntax: FOR name IN [ REVERSE ] a .. b [ BY step ] LOOP … END LOOP;

keywords.name: FOREACH
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, loops over the elements of an array.
keywords.syntax: FOREACH target [ SLICE n ] IN ARRAY expression LOOP … END LOOP;

keywords.name: WHILE
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, repeats statements while a condition is true.
keywords.syntax: WHILE condition LOOP … END LOOP;

keywords.name: EXIT
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, leaves a loop or labeled block, optionally only when a condition holds.
keywords.syntax: EXIT [ label ] [ WHEN condition ];

keywords.name: CONTINUE
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, skips to the next iteration of a loop.
keywords.syntax: CONTINUE [ label ] [ WHEN condition ];

keywords.name: RETURN
keywords.doc: In a function, returns a value, or with RETURN NEXT / RETURN QUERY adds rows to a set-returning function's result.
keywords.syntax: RETURN expression; | RETURN NEXT expression; | RETURN QUERY query;

keywords.name: ELSIF
keywords.doc: In PL/pgSQL, adds another condition to an IF statement.
keywords.syntax: IF … THEN … ELSIF condition THEN … END IF;

keywords.name: ON CONFLICT
keywords.doc: Specifies what INSERT does when a row would violate a unique or exclusion constraint.
keywords.syntax: INSERT … ON CONFLICT [ ( column [, …] ) | ON CONSTRAINT name ] DO { NOTHING | UPDATE SET … [ WHERE … ] }

keywords.name: CONFLICT
keywords.doc: Used in INSERT … ON CONFLICT.

keywords.name: DO NOTHING
keywords.doc: In ON CONFLICT, skips rows that would conflict.
keywords.syntax: INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING

keywords.name: NOTHING
keywords.doc: Used in ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and MERGE … THEN DO NOTHING.

keywords.name: DO UPDATE
keywords.doc: In ON CONFLICT, updates the existing conflicting row instead; the proposed row is available as EXCLUDED.
keywords.syntax: ON CONFLICT ( key ) DO UPDATE SET col = EXCLUDED.col [ WHERE … ]

keywords.name: EXCLUDED
keywords.doc: In ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, the special table holding the row that was proposed for insertion.
keywords.syntax: SET col = EXCLUDED.col

keywords.name: NULLS FIRST
keywords.doc: Sorts null values before non-null values.
keywords.syntax: ORDER BY expression [ ASC | DESC ] NULLS FIRST

keywords.name: NULLS LAST
keywords.doc: Sorts null values after non-null values.
keywords.syntax: ORDER BY expression [ ASC | DESC ] NULLS LAST

keywords.name: NULLS
keywords.doc: Used in NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST ordering and NULLS NOT DISTINCT unique constraints.

keywords.name: NULLS NOT DISTINCT
keywords.doc: Makes a unique constraint or index treat nulls as equal, so only one null is allowed. (PostgreSQL 15+)
keywords.syntax: UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT ( column [, …] )

keywords.name: DISTINCT ON
keywords.doc: Keeps only the first row of each group of rows with equal values of the given expressions, as ordered by ORDER BY.
keywords.syntax: SELECT DISTINCT ON ( expression [, …] ) … ORDER BY expression, …

keywords.name: TABLESAMPLE
keywords.doc: Returns a random sample of a table's rows.
keywords.syntax: FROM table TABLESAMPLE { BERNOULLI | SYSTEM } ( percent ) [ REPEATABLE ( seed ) ]

keywords.name: BERNOULLI
keywords.doc: A TABLESAMPLE method that picks each row independently with the given probability.

keywords.name: REPEATABLE
keywords.doc: In TABLESAMPLE, sets the seed so the same sample is returned each time. Also an isolation level (REPEATABLE READ).
keywords.syntax: TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI ( 10 ) REPEATABLE ( 42 )

keywords.name: GRANT
keywords.doc: Gives privileges on an object, or membership in a role, to roles.
keywords.syntax: GRANT privilege [, …] ON object TO role [, …] [ WITH GRANT OPTION ]

keywords.name: REVOKE
keywords.doc: Removes previously granted privileges or role memberships.
keywords.syntax: REVOKE [ GRANT OPTION FOR ] privilege [, …] ON object FROM role [, …] [ CASCADE | RESTRICT ]

keywords.name: PRIVILEGES
keywords.doc: Used in GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES.
keywords.syntax: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON table TO role

keywords.name: PUBLIC
keywords.doc: A pseudo-role meaning every role, used in GRANT and REVOKE.
keywords.syntax: GRANT SELECT ON table TO PUBLIC

keywords.name: USAGE
keywords.doc: A privilege that allows using a schema, sequence, type, language or foreign server.
keywords.syntax: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA name TO role

keywords.name: OWNER
keywords.doc: The role that owns an object and can alter or drop it.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE name OWNER TO new_owner

keywords.name: OWNER TO
keywords.doc: Changes the owner of an object.
keywords.syntax: ALTER object_type name OWNER TO { new_owner | CURRENT_USER | SESSION_USER }

keywords.name: OWNED BY
keywords.doc: Ties a sequence to a table column so it is dropped with the column, or in REASSIGN/DROP OWNED selects objects by owner.
keywords.syntax: ALTER SEQUENCE name OWNED BY table.column

keywords.name: ROLE
keywords.doc: A user or group that can own objects and hold privileges.
keywords.syntax: CREATE ROLE name [ [ WITH ] LOGIN | PASSWORD 'pw' | SUPERUSER | … ]

keywords.name: AUTHORIZATION
keywords.doc: Names the owner of a new schema, or sets the session user.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SCHEMA name AUTHORIZATION role

keywords.name: EXTENSION
keywords.doc: A packaged set of SQL objects, such as pgcrypto or postgis, installed into a database.
keywords.syntax: CREATE EXTENSION [ IF NOT EXISTS ] name [ WITH ] [ SCHEMA schema ] [ VERSION v ] [ CASCADE ]

keywords.name: MATERIALIZED VIEW
keywords.doc: A view whose query result is stored and must be refreshed explicitly.
keywords.syntax: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW [ IF NOT EXISTS ] name AS query [ WITH [ NO ] DATA ]

keywords.name: MATERIALIZED
keywords.doc: Used in MATERIALIZED VIEW, and in WITH name AS [ NOT ] MATERIALIZED to control CTE inlining.
keywords.syntax: WITH w AS MATERIALIZED ( … )

keywords.name: REFRESH
keywords.doc: Replaces the contents of a materialized view by re-running its query.
keywords.syntax: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW [ CONCURRENTLY ] name [ WITH [ NO ] DATA ]

keywords.name: CONCURRENTLY
keywords.doc: Builds an index or refreshes a materialized view without blocking concurrent reads and writes.
keywords.syntax: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY name ON table ( column )

keywords.name: VACUUM
keywords.doc: Reclaims storage from dead rows and optionally updates planner statistics.
keywords.syntax: VACUUM [ ( FULL, FREEZE, VERBOSE, ANALYZE, … ) ] [ table [ ( column [, …] ) ] [, …] ]

keywords.name: ANALYZE
keywords.doc: Collects statistics about table contents for the query planner. As an EXPLAIN option, runs the query and shows actual times.
keywords.syntax: ANALYZE [ VERBOSE ] [ table [ ( column [, …] ) ] [, …] ]

keywords.name: EXPLAIN
keywords.doc: Shows the execution plan for a statement; ANALYZE runs it and reports actual row counts and timings.
keywords.syntax: EXPLAIN [ ( ANALYZE, VERBOSE, COSTS, BUFFERS, FORMAT { TEXT | JSON | XML | YAML }, … ) ] statement

keywords.name: VERBOSE
keywords.doc: Requests more detailed output from EXPLAIN, VACUUM or ANALYZE.

keywords.name: COPY
keywords.doc: Copies data between a table or query and a file, program or the client.
keywords.syntax: COPY table [ ( column [, …] ) ] { FROM | TO } { 'file' | PROGRAM 'cmd' | STDIN | STDOUT } [ [ WITH ] ( FORMAT csv, HEADER, … ) ]

keywords.name: STDIN
keywords.doc: In COPY FROM, reads data sent by the client.
keywords.syntax: COPY table FROM STDIN

keywords.name: STDOUT
keywords.doc: In COPY TO, sends data to the client.
keywords.syntax: COPY table TO STDOUT

keywords.name: LISTEN
keywords.doc: Registers the session to receive notifications on a channel.
keywords.syntax: LISTEN channel

keywords.name: UNLISTEN
keywords.doc: Stops listening on a channel, or on all channels with *.
keywords.syntax: UNLISTEN { channel | * }

keywords.name: NOTIFY
keywords.doc: Sends a notification with an optional payload to every session listening on a channel.
keywords.syntax: NOTIFY channel [ , 'payload' ]

keywords.name: SHOW
keywords.doc: Displays the current value of a configuration setting.
keywords.syntax: SHOW { name | ALL }

keywords.name: RESET
keywords.doc: Restores a configuration setting to its default value.
keywords.syntax: RESET { name | ALL }

keywords.name: DISCARD
keywords.doc: Discards session state such as prepared statements, temporary tables or cached plans.
keywords.syntax: DISCARD { ALL | PLANS | SEQUENCES | TEMPORARY | TEMP }

keywords.name: LOCAL
keywords.doc: With SET, limits a setting change to the current transaction.
keywords.syntax: SET LOCAL name TO value

keywords.name: SESSION
keywords.doc: With SET, applies a setting for the rest of the session (the default).
keywords.syntax: SET SESSION name TO value

keywords.name: ARRAY
keywords.doc: Constructs an array from a list of values or from the results of a subquery.
keywords.syntax: ARRAY[ value [, …] ] | ARRAY( subquery )

keywords.name: INTERVAL
keywords.doc: Writes an interval literal, or names the interval data type.
keywords.syntax: INTERVAL '1 day 2 hours' | INTERVAL '3' MONTH

keywords.name: AT TIME ZONE
keywords.doc: Converts a timestamp to or from the given time zone.
keywords.syntax: timestamp_expression AT TIME ZONE zone

keywords.name: AT LOCAL
keywords.doc: Converts a timestamp using the session time zone, like AT TIME ZONE current_setting('TimeZone'). (PostgreSQL 17+)
keywords.syntax: timestamp_expression AT LOCAL

keywords.name: ZONE
keywords.doc: Used in AT TIME ZONE and in the type names WITH / WITHOUT TIME ZONE.

keywords.name: IS DISTINCT FROM
keywords.doc: Compares two values treating null as a normal value: true when they differ, never null.
keywords.syntax: a IS DISTINCT FROM b

keywords.name: IS NOT DISTINCT FROM
keywords.doc: Compares two values treating null as a normal value: true when they are equal or both null.
keywords.syntax: a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b

keywords.name: GENERATED
keywords.doc: Defines an identity column or a generated (computed) column.
keywords.syntax: column type GENERATED { ALWAYS | BY DEFAULT } AS IDENTITY | GENERATED ALWAYS AS ( expression ) STORED

keywords.name: ALWAYS
keywords.doc: In an identity column, rejects user-supplied values unless OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE is used; also used for stored generated columns.

keywords.name: IDENTITY
keywords.doc: An auto-numbered column backed by an implicit sequence.
keywords.syntax: id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY

keywords.name: STORED
keywords.doc: Marks a generated column as computed on write and stored on disk.
keywords.syntax: total numeric GENERATED ALWAYS AS ( price * qty ) STORED

keywords.name: OVERRIDING
keywords.doc: In INSERT, lets explicit values be written to an identity column (SYSTEM VALUE) or ignored in favor of the sequence (USER VALUE).
keywords.syntax: INSERT INTO t OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE VALUES ( … )

keywords.name: OVERLAPS
keywords.doc: Tests whether two time periods overlap.
keywords.syntax: ( start1, end1 ) OVERLAPS ( start2, end2 )

keywords.name: SYMMETRIC
keywords.doc: Makes BETWEEN accept its bounds in either order.
keywords.syntax: x BETWEEN SYMMETRIC a AND b

keywords.name: ASYMMETRIC
keywords.doc: The default BETWEEN behavior, where the first bound must be the lower one.

keywords.name: CHECKPOINT
keywords.doc: Forces an immediate write-ahead log checkpoint.
keywords.syntax: CHECKPOINT

keywords.name: LOCK
keywords.doc: Explicitly locks a table for the rest of the transaction.
keywords.syntax: LOCK [ TABLE ] [ ONLY ] name [ IN lock_mode MODE ] [ NOWAIT ]

keywords.name: SKIP LOCKED
keywords.doc: In a row-locking clause, skips rows that are locked by other transactions instead of waiting.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED

keywords.name: SKIP
keywords.doc: Used in FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

keywords.name: LOCKED
keywords.doc: Used in FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

keywords.name: NOWAIT
keywords.doc: Reports an error instead of waiting when a row or table lock cannot be acquired immediately.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FOR UPDATE NOWAIT

keywords.name: FOR UPDATE
keywords.doc: Locks the selected rows against concurrent updates and deletes until the transaction ends.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FOR UPDATE [ OF table [, …] ] [ NOWAIT | SKIP LOCKED ]

keywords.name: FOR NO KEY UPDATE
keywords.doc: Like FOR UPDATE but weaker: does not block FOR KEY SHARE locks, as used by foreign key checks.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FOR NO KEY UPDATE

keywords.name: FOR SHARE
keywords.doc: Locks the selected rows against updates and deletes while allowing other shared locks.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FOR SHARE [ NOWAIT | SKIP LOCKED ]

keywords.name: FOR KEY SHARE
keywords.doc: The weakest row lock: blocks deletes and key changes but not other updates.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FOR KEY SHARE

keywords.name: SHARE
keywords.doc: Used in FOR SHARE row locks and SHARE table lock modes.

keywords.name: OF
keywords.doc: Names the tables a row-locking clause applies to, or in a trigger, the columns an UPDATE trigger watches.
keywords.syntax: FOR UPDATE OF table

keywords.name: INHERITS
keywords.doc: Makes a new table inherit all columns of one or more parent tables.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE child ( … ) INHERITS ( parent [, …] )

keywords.name: COMMENT
keywords.doc: Stores a comment on a database object.
keywords.syntax: COMMENT ON { TABLE | COLUMN | FUNCTION | … } name IS 'text'

keywords.name: COMMENT ON
keywords.doc: Stores or replaces the comment on a database object.
keywords.syntax: COMMENT ON TABLE name IS 'text'

keywords.name: RENAME
keywords.doc: Renames an object or column in an ALTER statement.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE name RENAME [ COLUMN ] old TO new

keywords.name: TO
keywords.doc: Used in RENAME … TO, OWNER TO, GRANT … TO and ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT.

keywords.name: TYPE
keywords.doc: A user-defined data type: composite, enum, range or base type. In ALTER COLUMN, changes a column's type.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TYPE name AS ( field type [, …] ) | AS ENUM ( 'a', 'b' ) | AS RANGE ( SUBTYPE = type )

keywords.name: ENUM
keywords.doc: Defines an enumerated type with a fixed, ordered list of labels.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TYPE name AS ENUM ( 'label' [, …] )

keywords.name: DOMAIN
keywords.doc: A data type based on another type with optional constraints.
keywords.syntax: CREATE DOMAIN name AS type [ DEFAULT expr ] [ CHECK ( VALUE > 0 ) ]

keywords.name: COLLATION
keywords.doc: Defines sort order and character classification rules for text.
keywords.syntax: CREATE COLLATION name ( provider = icu, locale = 'de-DE' )

keywords.name: TABLESPACE
keywords.doc: A storage location on disk for tables and indexes.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLESPACE name LOCATION 'directory'

keywords.name: RULE
keywords.doc: A query rewrite rule attached to a table or view.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] RULE name AS ON event TO table DO [ ALSO | INSTEAD ] …

keywords.name: POLICY
keywords.doc: A row-level security policy that restricts which rows a role can see or modify.
keywords.syntax: CREATE POLICY name ON table [ FOR command ] [ TO role ] USING ( condition ) [ WITH CHECK ( condition ) ]

keywords.name: PUBLICATION
keywords.doc: A set of tables whose changes are published for logical replication.
keywords.syntax: CREATE PUBLICATION name FOR TABLE table [, …] | FOR ALL TABLES

keywords.name: SUBSCRIPTION
keywords.doc: A logical replication subscription to a publication on another server.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SUBSCRIPTION name CONNECTION 'conninfo' PUBLICATION pub

keywords.name: GROUPING SETS
keywords.doc: Groups by several sets of columns in one query, like a UNION ALL of GROUP BYs.
keywords.syntax: GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ( ( a, b ), ( a ), () )

keywords.name: ROLLUP
keywords.doc: Groups by each prefix of the listed expressions, adding subtotal and grand-total rows.
keywords.syntax: GROUP BY ROLLUP ( a, b, c )

keywords.name: CUBE
keywords.doc: Groups by every combination of the listed expressions.
keywords.syntax: GROUP BY CUBE ( a, b )

keywords.name: WITH ORDINALITY
keywords.doc: Adds a bigint column numbering the rows returned by a set-returning function in FROM.
keywords.syntax: FROM unnest( array ) WITH ORDINALITY AS t( value, n )

keywords.name: ORDINALITY
keywords.doc: Used in WITH ORDINALITY.

keywords.name: MERGE
keywords.doc: Conditionally inserts, updates or deletes rows of a target table based on a join with a source.
keywords.syntax: MERGE INTO target USING source ON condition WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET … WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT …

keywords.name: MERGE INTO
keywords.doc: Starts a MERGE statement on the given target table.
keywords.syntax: MERGE INTO target [ AS alias ] USING source ON condition …

keywords.name: MATCHED
keywords.doc: Used in MERGE WHEN [ NOT ] MATCHED clauses.

keywords.name: WHEN MATCHED
keywords.doc: In MERGE, the action for target rows that have a matching source row.
keywords.syntax: WHEN MATCHED [ AND condition ] THEN { UPDATE SET … | DELETE | DO NOTHING }

keywords.name: WHEN NOT MATCHED
keywords.doc: In MERGE, the action for source rows with no matching target row (or, BY SOURCE, target rows with no source row).
keywords.syntax: WHEN NOT MATCHED [ BY TARGET ] [ AND condition ] THEN INSERT …

keywords.name: DEFERRABLE
keywords.doc: Allows a constraint's check to be postponed to the end of the transaction.
keywords.syntax: … REFERENCES t ( id ) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED

keywords.name: INITIALLY DEFERRED
keywords.doc: Makes a deferrable constraint checked at transaction end by default.

keywords.name: INITIALLY IMMEDIATE
keywords.doc: Makes a deferrable constraint checked after each statement by default.

keywords.name: SET CONSTRAINTS
keywords.doc: Changes when deferrable constraints are checked in the current transaction.
keywords.syntax: SET CONSTRAINTS { ALL | name [, …] } { DEFERRED | IMMEDIATE }

keywords.name: NO ACTION
keywords.doc: Foreign key action that raises an error if referencing rows remain when the check runs (the default).
keywords.syntax: ON DELETE NO ACTION

keywords.name: ACTION
keywords.doc: Used in the foreign key action NO ACTION.

keywords.name: EXCLUDE
keywords.doc: Defines an exclusion constraint: no two rows may satisfy all the given operator comparisons.
keywords.syntax: EXCLUDE USING gist ( room WITH =, during WITH && )

keywords.name: NOT VALID
keywords.doc: Adds a foreign key or check constraint without checking existing rows; validate later with VALIDATE CONSTRAINT.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT c … NOT VALID

keywords.name: VALIDATE
keywords.doc: Checks existing rows against a constraint that was added as NOT VALID.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t VALIDATE CONSTRAINT name

keywords.name: ISOLATION LEVEL
keywords.doc: Sets the transaction isolation level.
keywords.syntax: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL { SERIALIZABLE | REPEATABLE READ | READ COMMITTED | READ UNCOMMITTED }

keywords.name: SERIALIZABLE
keywords.doc: The strictest isolation level: transactions behave as if run one at a time.

keywords.name: REPEATABLE READ
keywords.doc: An isolation level where every statement in the transaction sees the same snapshot.

keywords.name: READ COMMITTED
keywords.doc: The default isolation level: each statement sees data committed before it began.

keywords.name: READ UNCOMMITTED
keywords.doc: Accepted for compatibility; behaves like READ COMMITTED in PostgreSQL.

keywords.name: READ ONLY
keywords.doc: Makes a transaction unable to modify data.
keywords.syntax: BEGIN READ ONLY

keywords.name: READ WRITE
keywords.doc: Allows a transaction to modify data (the default).

keywords.name: START TRANSACTION
keywords.doc: Begins a transaction block, like BEGIN.
keywords.syntax: START TRANSACTION [ ISOLATION LEVEL … ] [ READ WRITE | READ ONLY ] [ [ NOT ] DEFERRABLE ]

keywords.name: WORK
keywords.doc: Optional noise word in BEGIN WORK, COMMIT WORK and ROLLBACK WORK.

keywords.name: RELEASE
keywords.doc: Destroys a savepoint, keeping the effects of commands run after it.
keywords.syntax: RELEASE [ SAVEPOINT ] name

keywords.name: ROLLBACK TO
keywords.doc: Undoes all commands run after a savepoint, keeping the savepoint.
keywords.syntax: ROLLBACK TO [ SAVEPOINT ] name

keywords.name: PREPARE
keywords.doc: Creates a prepared statement, or with PREPARE TRANSACTION prepares the current transaction for two-phase commit.
keywords.syntax: PREPARE name [ ( type [, …] ) ] AS statement

keywords.name: DEALLOCATE
keywords.doc: Removes a prepared statement.
keywords.syntax: DEALLOCATE [ PREPARE ] { name | ALL }

keywords.name: CLUSTER
keywords.doc: Physically reorders a table according to an index.
keywords.syntax: CLUSTER [ VERBOSE ] [ table [ USING index ] ]

keywords.name: REINDEX
keywords.doc: Rebuilds indexes.
keywords.syntax: REINDEX [ ( CONCURRENTLY, VERBOSE ) ] { INDEX | TABLE | SCHEMA | DATABASE | SYSTEM } name

keywords.name: CURSOR
keywords.doc: A named pointer into a query result that can be fetched from incrementally.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE name CURSOR [ WITH HOLD ] FOR query

keywords.name: CLOSE
keywords.doc: Closes an open cursor.
keywords.syntax: CLOSE { name | ALL }

keywords.name: MOVE
keywords.doc: Repositions a cursor without returning rows.
keywords.syntax: MOVE [ direction ] [ FROM | IN ] cursor

keywords.name: BEFORE
keywords.doc: Fires a trigger before the operation on each row or statement.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name BEFORE INSERT ON table …

keywords.name: AFTER
keywords.doc: Fires a trigger after the operation on each row or statement.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name AFTER UPDATE ON table …

keywords.name: INSTEAD OF
keywords.doc: Fires a trigger on a view in place of the INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name INSTEAD OF INSERT ON view FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION f()

keywords.name: INSTEAD
keywords.doc: Used in INSTEAD OF triggers and DO INSTEAD rules.

keywords.name: FOR EACH ROW
keywords.doc: Fires a trigger once for every affected row.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER … FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION f()

keywords.name: FOR EACH STATEMENT
keywords.doc: Fires a trigger once per statement, regardless of how many rows it affects (the default).

keywords.name: EACH
keywords.doc: Used in FOR EACH ROW / FOR EACH STATEMENT.

keywords.name: STATEMENT
keywords.doc: Used in FOR EACH STATEMENT triggers.

keywords.name: EXECUTE FUNCTION
keywords.doc: Names the function a trigger calls.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER … EXECUTE FUNCTION function_name ( [ arguments ] )

keywords.name: REFERENCING
keywords.doc: In a statement-level trigger, names transition tables holding the old and new rows.
keywords.syntax: REFERENCING OLD TABLE AS old_rows NEW TABLE AS new_rows

keywords.name: ENABLE
keywords.doc: Turns on a trigger, rule or row-level security in ALTER TABLE.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE name ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY

keywords.name: DISABLE
keywords.doc: Turns off a trigger, rule or row-level security in ALTER TABLE.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE name DISABLE TRIGGER { name | ALL | USER }

keywords.name: ATTACH PARTITION
keywords.doc: Attaches an existing table as a partition of a partitioned table.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE parent ATTACH PARTITION child FOR VALUES FROM ( … ) TO ( … )

keywords.name: DETACH PARTITION
keywords.doc: Detaches a partition, turning it into a standalone table.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE parent DETACH PARTITION child [ CONCURRENTLY | FINALIZE ]

keywords.name: ATTACH
keywords.doc: Used in ALTER TABLE … ATTACH PARTITION.

keywords.name: DETACH
keywords.doc: Used in ALTER TABLE … DETACH PARTITION.

keywords.name: PARTITION OF
keywords.doc: Creates a table as a partition of a partitioned table.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE child PARTITION OF parent FOR VALUES { IN ( … ) | FROM ( … ) TO ( … ) | WITH ( MODULUS m, REMAINDER r ) }

keywords.name: INCLUDE
keywords.doc: Adds non-key payload columns to an index for index-only scans.
keywords.syntax: CREATE INDEX name ON table ( key ) INCLUDE ( column [, …] )

keywords.name: DEFAULT VALUES
keywords.doc: Inserts one row using each column's default value.
keywords.syntax: INSERT INTO table DEFAULT VALUES

keywords.name: CYCLE
keywords.doc: Lets a sequence wrap around at its limit. In a recursive CTE, detects cycles.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SEQUENCE s CYCLE | WITH RECURSIVE … CYCLE id SET is_cycle USING path

keywords.name: INCREMENT
keywords.doc: Sets the step of a sequence.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SEQUENCE name INCREMENT BY n

keywords.name: MINVALUE
keywords.doc: Sets the minimum value of a sequence.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SEQUENCE name MINVALUE n

keywords.name: MAXVALUE
keywords.doc: Sets the maximum value of a sequence.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SEQUENCE name MAXVALUE n

keywords.name: RESTART
keywords.doc: Resets a sequence, or with TRUNCATE … RESTART IDENTITY resets the owned sequences.
keywords.syntax: ALTER SEQUENCE name RESTART [ WITH n ]

keywords.name: PLACING
keywords.doc: Used in overlay(string PLACING replacement FROM start FOR count).

keywords.name: LEADING
keywords.doc: In trim(), removes characters from the start of the string only.
keywords.syntax: trim(LEADING 'x' FROM string)

keywords.name: TRAILING
keywords.doc: In trim(), removes characters from the end of the string only.
keywords.syntax: trim(TRAILING 'x' FROM string)

keywords.name: BOTH
keywords.doc: In trim(), removes characters from both ends of the string (the default).
keywords.syntax: trim(BOTH 'x' FROM string)

keywords.name: PASSING
keywords.doc: Supplies the input document and variables to xmltable, xmlexists and the SQL/JSON query functions.

constants.name: TRUE
constants.doc: The boolean true value. PostgreSQL also accepts 't', 'true', 'yes', 'on' and '1' as boolean input strings.

constants.name: FALSE
constants.doc: The boolean false value. PostgreSQL also accepts 'f', 'false', 'no', 'off' and '0' as boolean input strings.

constants.name: UNKNOWN
constants.doc: The third boolean truth value, represented by null; used in IS [ NOT ] UNKNOWN.

types.name: smallint
types.doc: Signed 2-byte integer, from -32768 to 32767. Alias int2.

types.name: int2
types.doc: Alias for smallint: signed 2-byte integer.

types.name: integer
types.doc: Signed 4-byte integer, from about -2.1 billion to 2.1 billion. Aliases int and int4.

types.name: int
types.doc: Alias for integer: signed 4-byte integer.

types.name: int4
types.doc: Alias for integer: signed 4-byte integer.

types.name: bigint
types.doc: Signed 8-byte integer, from about -9.2e18 to 9.2e18. Alias int8.

types.name: int8
types.doc: Alias for bigint: signed 8-byte integer.

types.name: smallserial
types.doc: Auto-incrementing 2-byte integer backed by a sequence. Alias serial2.

types.name: serial2
types.doc: Alias for smallserial: auto-incrementing 2-byte integer.

types.name: serial
types.doc: Auto-incrementing 4-byte integer backed by a sequence. Alias serial4. Identity columns are the SQL-standard alternative.

types.name: serial4
types.doc: Alias for serial: auto-incrementing 4-byte integer.

types.name: bigserial
types.doc: Auto-incrementing 8-byte integer backed by a sequence. Alias serial8.

types.name: serial8
types.doc: Alias for bigserial: auto-incrementing 8-byte integer.

types.name: numeric
types.doc: Exact number with user-specified precision (total digits) and scale (digits after the point). Without arguments, any precision up to the implementation limit.

types.name: decimal
types.doc: Alias for numeric: exact number with user-specified precision and scale.

types.name: real
types.doc: 4-byte floating-point number with about 6 decimal digits of precision. Alias float4.

types.name: float4
types.doc: Alias for real: 4-byte floating-point number.

types.name: double
types.doc: double precision: 8-byte floating-point number with about 15 decimal digits of precision. Alias float8.

types.name: float8
types.doc: Alias for double precision: 8-byte floating-point number.

types.name: float
types.doc: Floating-point number; float(1) to float(24) is real, float(25) to float(53) and plain float are double precision.

types.name: money
types.doc: Currency amount with fixed fractional precision determined by the lc_monetary setting.

types.name: character
types.doc: Fixed-length, blank-padded text. character varying(n) is the variable-length form (varchar). Alias char.

types.name: char
types.doc: Fixed-length, blank-padded text of n characters (1 if omitted). Alias for character.

types.name: bpchar
types.doc: Blank-padded character type underlying char(n); without a length it accepts any length.

types.name: varchar
types.doc: Variable-length text with an optional length limit n. Alias for character varying.

types.name: text
types.doc: Variable-length text of unlimited length.

types.name: name
types.doc: 63-byte type used internally for identifiers in the system catalogs.

types.name: bytea
types.doc: Variable-length binary string.

types.name: boolean
types.doc: Logical true/false value, which may also be null (unknown). Alias bool.

types.name: bool
types.doc: Alias for boolean.

types.name: date
types.doc: Calendar date (year, month, day) with no time of day.

types.name: time
types.doc: Time of day, without time zone unless WITH TIME ZONE is given; p is fractional-second digits (0 to 6).
types.syntax: time [ ( p ) ] [ { WITH | WITHOUT } TIME ZONE ]

types.name: timetz
types.doc: Alias for time with time zone: time of day with a UTC offset. Rarely useful; prefer timestamptz.

types.name: timestamp
types.doc: Date and time, without time zone unless WITH TIME ZONE is given; p is fractional-second digits (0 to 6).
types.syntax: timestamp [ ( p ) ] [ { WITH | WITHOUT } TIME ZONE ]

types.name: timestamptz
types.doc: Alias for timestamp with time zone: an absolute point in time, stored as UTC and displayed in the session time zone.

types.name: interval
types.doc: Time span in months, days and microseconds, optionally restricted to certain fields.

types.name: uuid
types.doc: Universally unique identifier (128 bits), written as 32 hexadecimal digits in groups.

types.name: json
types.doc: JSON data stored as text, preserving whitespace, key order and duplicate keys.

types.name: jsonb
types.doc: JSON data stored in a decomposed binary form: faster to query and indexable, without duplicate keys or key order.

types.name: jsonpath
types.doc: An SQL/JSON path expression, as used by jsonb_path_query and related functions.

types.name: xml
types.doc: XML data, checked for well-formedness.

types.name: inet
types.doc: IPv4 or IPv6 host address with an optional netmask.

types.name: cidr
types.doc: IPv4 or IPv6 network specification; host bits to the right of the netmask must be zero.

types.name: macaddr
types.doc: 6-byte MAC address.

types.name: macaddr8
types.doc: 8-byte MAC address in EUI-64 format.

types.name: point
types.doc: Geometric point (x, y) on a plane.

types.name: line
types.doc: Infinite geometric line, stored as {A, B, C} for Ax + By + C = 0.

types.name: lseg
types.doc: Finite geometric line segment between two points.

types.name: box
types.doc: Rectangular box given by two opposite corners.

types.name: path
types.doc: Geometric path of points, open or closed.

types.name: polygon
types.doc: Closed geometric polygon.

types.name: circle
types.doc: Geometric circle given by a center point and radius.

types.name: tsvector
types.doc: A sorted list of distinct lexemes, optionally with positions and weights, used for full-text search.

types.name: tsquery
types.doc: A full-text search query of lexemes combined with & (and), | (or), ! (not) and <-> (followed by).

types.name: bit
types.doc: Fixed-length bit string of n bits (1 if omitted). bit varying(n) is the variable-length form.

types.name: varbit
types.doc: Alias for bit varying: variable-length bit string with an optional maximum length.

types.name: int4range
types.doc: Range of integer.

types.name: int8range
types.doc: Range of bigint.

types.name: numrange
types.doc: Range of numeric.

types.name: tsrange
types.doc: Range of timestamp without time zone.

types.name: tstzrange
types.doc: Range of timestamp with time zone.

types.name: daterange
types.doc: Range of date.

types.name: int4multirange
types.doc: Multirange (ordered set of non-overlapping ranges) of integer. (PostgreSQL 14+)

types.name: int8multirange
types.doc: Multirange of bigint. (PostgreSQL 14+)

types.name: nummultirange
types.doc: Multirange of numeric. (PostgreSQL 14+)

types.name: tsmultirange
types.doc: Multirange of timestamp without time zone. (PostgreSQL 14+)

types.name: tstzmultirange
types.doc: Multirange of timestamp with time zone. (PostgreSQL 14+)

types.name: datemultirange
types.doc: Multirange of date. (PostgreSQL 14+)

types.name: oid
types.doc: Unsigned 4-byte object identifier used as the primary key of system catalogs.

types.name: regclass
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a relation name, such as 'orders'::regclass.

types.name: regtype
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a data type name.

types.name: regproc
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a function name.

types.name: regprocedure
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a function name with argument types.

types.name: regoper
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints an operator name.

types.name: regoperator
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints an operator with argument types.

types.name: regrole
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a role name.

types.name: regnamespace
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a schema name.

types.name: regconfig
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a text search configuration name.

types.name: regdictionary
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a text search dictionary name.

types.name: regcollation
types.doc: OID alias type that reads and prints a collation name.

types.name: xid
types.doc: 32-bit transaction identifier.

types.name: xid8
types.doc: 64-bit transaction identifier that does not wrap around.

types.name: cid
types.doc: Command identifier within a transaction.

types.name: tid
types.doc: Tuple identifier: the physical location (block, offset) of a row version, as in the ctid system column.

types.name: pg_lsn
types.doc: Write-ahead log location (log sequence number).

types.name: pg_snapshot
types.doc: Transaction snapshot: which transaction IDs were in progress at a point in time.

types.name: txid_snapshot
types.doc: Older form of pg_snapshot using bigint transaction IDs; deprecated.

types.name: refcursor
types.doc: A reference to a cursor, used to return cursors from PL/pgSQL functions.

types.name: record
types.doc: Pseudo-type for a row of unspecified structure, as returned by functions without a declared row type.

types.name: void
types.doc: Pseudo-type for a function that returns no value.

types.name: anyelement
types.doc: Polymorphic pseudo-type: a function parameter that accepts any type.

types.name: anyarray
types.doc: Polymorphic pseudo-type: a function parameter that accepts any array type.

types.name: anynonarray
types.doc: Polymorphic pseudo-type: a function parameter that accepts any non-array type.

types.name: anyenum
types.doc: Polymorphic pseudo-type: a function parameter that accepts any enum type.

types.name: anyrange
types.doc: Polymorphic pseudo-type: a function parameter that accepts any range type.

types.name: anymultirange
types.doc: Polymorphic pseudo-type: a function parameter that accepts any multirange type.

types.name: anycompatible
types.doc: Polymorphic pseudo-type that accepts any type, with arguments promoted to a common type.

types.name: anycompatiblearray
types.doc: Polymorphic pseudo-type that accepts any array, with arguments promoted to a common type.

types.name: event_trigger
types.doc: Pseudo-type returned by event trigger functions.
